optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Product Requirements Analyst, Collaboration Software Subscriptions

professionalSummary.text: Product Requirements Analyst with two years of experience on a subscription product team focused on self-service billing and seat-management pages for business customers.
professionalSummary.witness: Two years on the subscription product team covering intake, story writing, acceptance sessions and release notes for the self-service billing pages.

experienceHighlights.text: Turned weekly intake from subscription operations and customer success into user stories with acceptance criteria for self-service seat-change and invoice-download pages.
experienceHighlights.witness: Turned the weekly intake from subscription operations and customer success into user stories for the self-service seat-change and invoice-download pages, each story carrying its acceptance criteria.

experienceHighlights.text: Led acceptance sessions for three billing-page releases, logging pass/fail criteria with operations analysts and customer success managers.
experienceHighlights.witness: Led acceptance sessions for three billing-page releases with two operations analysts and a customer success manager, logging every criterion as passed or failed.

experienceHighlights.text: Agreed release scope with engineering and subscription operations, documenting decisions made during sprint planning.
experienceHighlights.witness: Agreed release scope in sprint planning with the engineering manager and the subscription operations lead; scope and the release date were the engineering manager's call.

experienceHighlights.text: Published release notes detailing limitations and support team handover requirements for self-service features.
experienceHighlights.witness: Published release notes for the seat-change and invoice-download pages that spelled out one limitation (invoices older than twelve months could not be downloaded) and what the support team needed to take over.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Work sample includes story set for invoice-download page with acceptance criteria and pass/fail log from acceptance session, with traceable ticket identifiers.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the story set for the invoice-download page with its acceptance criteria, plus the pass/fail log from one acceptance session; ticket identifiers are included so the entries can be traced.

skills.text: Self-service billing and seat-management page requirements gathering, user story writing, acceptance testing, and release notes publishing.
skills.witness: Two years on the subscription product team covering intake, story writing, acceptance sessions and release notes for the self-service billing pages.

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The materials establish the candidate's experience with requirements gathering, user story writing, acceptance sessions, release notes, and a work sample. The materials do not establish evidence of reduced billing support tickets as measured against a baseline.

decisionBoundary.statement: Human review required due to missing evidence for requirement req_3e46120095e0 (reduced billing support tickets).

role.roleTitle: Product Requirements Analyst, Collaboration Software Subscriptions

evidence.text: Turned the weekly intake from subscription operations and customer success into user stories for the self-service seat-change and invoice-download pages, each story carrying its acceptance criteria.
Led acceptance sessions for three billing-page releases with two operations analysts and a customer success manager, logging every criterion as passed or failed.

Recruiter screen: candidate said billing tickets 'fell by about 30 percent' after the invoice-download page launched; he said the support team had mentioned it in a stand-up and that he had not seen a ticket report himself.
evidence.notes: Anecdotal claim without documented baseline or measurement

missingEvidence: Documented reduction in billing support tickets

evidence.text: Agreed release scope in sprint planning with the engineering manager and the subscription operations lead; scope and the release date were the engineering manager's call.

Published release notes for the seat-change and invoice-download pages that spelled out one limitation (invoices older than twelve months could not be downloaded) and what the support team needed to take over.

supportedClaims.witness: Turned the weekly intake from subscription operations and customer success into user stories for the self-service seat-change and invoice-download pages, each story carrying its acceptance criteria.

supportedClaims.witness: Led acceptance sessions for three billing-page releases with two operations analysts and a customer success manager, logging every criterion as passed or failed.

supportedClaims.claim: Agreed release scope with engineering and subscription operations, documenting decisions made during sprint planning.
supportedClaims.witness: Agreed release scope in sprint planning with the engineering manager and the subscription operations lead; scope and the release date were the engineering manager's call.

supportedClaims.claim: Published release notes detailing limitations and support team handover requirements for self-service features.
supportedClaims.witness: Published release notes for the seat-change and invoice-download pages that spelled out one limitation (invoices older than twelve months could not be downloaded) and what the support team needed to take over.

unsupportedClaims.claim: Billing support tickets fell by 30 percent after the invoice-download page launched.
unsupportedClaims.reason: Claim is anecdotal and lacks documented baseline measurement.
unsupportedClaims.requiredFollowUp: Request documented ticket reports showing reduction against monthly baseline.

interviewSignalRisks.recommendedHandling: Verify with documented ticket reports and baseline data.

followUpQuestions.question: Can you provide documented evidence showing that delivered self-service features reduced billing support tickets, measured against the recorded monthly baseline?
followUpQuestions.evidenceTarget: Documented ticket reports showing reduction against monthly baseline

Check if the candidate can provide specific examples of ticket reduction
